template_instructions.doc_name_en: Subject Information and Consent Form - Impartial Witness
template_instructions.doc_name_local: Study Participant Information and Consent Form – Impartial Witness
template_instructions.description: Must be used when the study involves an adult participant who has capacity to consent but cannot read, write or sign the standard consent form. The participant decides personally, while an impartial witness confirms and documents the consent process.
footer: Protocol number: [fill in] | EU trial number: [fill in]
info_table: Data Protection Officer [name and contact details]
template_instructions.content_instructions: Tailor the document to the specific clinical trial; remove sections and alternatives that do not apply and add study-specific information needed for an informed decision. Use clear Irish English, plain language consistent with National Adult Literacy Agency principles, approximately a 12-year-old reading level where feasible, short paragraphs, descriptive headings and bullets. Spell out abbreviations on first use and explain unavoidable medical or technical terms. Keep the document consistent with the approved protocol, CTIS Part II dossier and Irish site arrangements. Describe research versus usual care, purpose, why the person is invited, procedures in the order experienced, duration, risks and burdens, possible benefits, alternatives where relevant, voluntariness and withdrawal, insurance/injury arrangements, costs/reimbursement, results, contacts and ethics approval. For Irish data protection, identify the personal data used, sources, controllers/processors/recipients, retention, security, medical-record access, transfers outside the EEA and participant-facing safeguards, rights, Data Protection Officer and complaint route; use a simple study-specific explanation of the GDPR lawful basis. Include explicit consent for processing health-research data as the default for capable participants; remove it only where an approved Irish alternative or consent-declaration route applies. For biological samples used within the main trial, state sample type and amount, whether collection/use is mandatory or optional, purpose, coding, storage location and duration, analyses, recipients/transfers, security and what happens after analysis or withdrawal. For genetic or genomic testing within the main trial, state whether it is mandatory or optional, the type and purpose of testing, limits to anonymity, foreseeable privacy/family risks, handling of individual or incidental findings, storage/security, transfers and any relevant commercial involvement. Required study procedures, required biological samples and required genetic/genomic testing must be clearly described and, when applicable, included in the Required acknowledgements list with an individual confirmation checkbox. Use separate Yes/No choices only for genuinely optional activities that may be refused without preventing the main activity covered by the form. Do not include optional storage or secondary/future research beyond the approved main-trial purposes; that belongs only in the separate Secondary and Future Use template. Use only when the adult participant has full decision-making capacity and personally decides but is unable to provide a written signature. The impartial witness does not consent on the participant’s behalf and must witness the consent process and consent obtained. Where information must be read or otherwise communicated to the participant, adapt the information-delivery method as needed. Preserve all main-trial information, sample/genetic logic and the participant’s own required/optional choices. Do not add incapacity, representative or deferred-consent language.
template_instructions.styling_instructions: Use clear participant-facing question headings and short sections. Use a clean readable font such as Calibri, Arial, Verdana or Tahoma at about 12 point. Avoid block capitals and unnecessary legalistic text. Use tables or simple flow charts when they improve understanding. Present required acknowledgements as a clear list with one checkbox beside each applicable acknowledgement and the final dated signature. Do not use Yes/No choices or initials for required acknowledgements. Use Yes/No choices only for genuinely optional components. Where optional components are included, present their confirmation/signature separately from the main consent signature. Use separate fields for printed name, date and signature.

template_content.section_content: You are being asked whether you want to take part in a clinical trial. You make the decision yourself. This version is used because you are unable to provide the usual written signature. The study information will be provided and explained in a way you can understand. An impartial witness will be present for the full information and consent discussion. The witness does not decide for you and does not consent on your behalf. You will have time to ask questions and decide.
template_content.section_style: Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Part 1 – The Research Project Why is this study being done? · Provide an outline of the purpose of your study in lay language. Do not cut and paste directly from the protocol. Pay particular attention to aspects that are experimental e.g. new medicinal products or medical devices or drugs being used outside their existing product licence. We are doing this study to …
template_content.section_style: Section break, H2 document subline, H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Why have I been invited to take part? · Explain specifically why that person has been invited (e.g. because they have a specific condition, or because they are a healthy individual). · State how many participants you are intending to involve and their characteristics (e.g. healthy volunteers, people with a specific condition or demographic). · Make sure that people with no medical training or background understand the words you use. Do not assume patients will understand words and terms such as ‘inclusion’, ‘exclusion criteria’ and ‘control’.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Do I have to take part? Can I withdraw? Explain: · that participation is voluntary; · that a decision not to consent will have no adverse consequences; · that consent can be withdrawn at any time. Advise when and how consent can be withdrawn (e.g. before anonymisation of the data or publication of results) and the effect of any such withdrawal. · the process of withdrawal, i.e. contact XXX on 01-XXXXXX SAMPLE TEXT: Example (for studies based in clinical care setting): You don't have to take part in this study. It is entirely voluntary. If you decide not to take part it won’t affect your current or future medical care. You can change your mind about taking part in the study and opt out at any time even if the study has started. If you decide to opt out, it won’t affect your current or future medical care. You don't have to give a reason for not taking part or for opting out. If you wish to opt out, please contact [insert name, role and contact details] who will be able to organise this for you.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What happens if I change my mind? Participation is voluntary and you may withdraw at any time without giving a reason or affecting your usual care. Explain exactly how to withdraw and any safety implications or final safety visit offered. Explain what happens to information and samples already collected. Do not promise that all research data can automatically be deleted: some information may need to remain for trial integrity, safety reporting or legal/regulatory requirements. For remaining identifiable biological samples, explain whether they can be destroyed or otherwise withdrawn from further main-trial use, and the limits where samples have already been analysed, used up or results generated.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: How will the study be carried out? Provide a general overview of the study. Important questions to address in this section include: · When will the study take place? · Where will the study will take? · What will happen in general terms? · How many patients will be taking part in the study?
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What will happen to me if I decide to take part? · This is a very important section. · Participants need to know exactly what they are consenting to. Keep the language simple. · This section details what will be involved in your research study from a participant’s point of view, and in the order they will experience it. · Details of the procedures and tests that will be performed – and by whom. · If there are multiple study visits, describe them in turn. · If research is taking place in the context of clinical care, make clear which parts are research and which standard care. · A table or flow chart can provide clarity when describing a complex series of interventions. · Clearly state what will be expected of the participant if s/he takes part with adequate detail regarding procedures, duration and location of testing/interviews etc. · Any procedures which are experimental should be identified and alternative procedures or courses of treatment disclosed. · Where involvement in the research involves a change to the ‘usual care’ this individual would receive, this should be specified. Consider: · Where will the participant have to go? · How long the participant will be involved in the research, how often they will need to attend a research session and how long visits will be. · If you will be allocating participants randomly to study medication(s) and/or placebo, describe what it means in lay terms. · Are any of the tests invasive? · If you will be collecting samples, give an idea of amounts. Blood volume may be more meaningfully expressed in tablespoons: 5ml is equivalent to 1 teaspoon, 15ml is 1 tablespoon. Biopsies may be compared to grains of rice. · If you will be using tissue samples, state whether the tissue will already be collected as part of clinical care. Are you requesting use of tissue surplus to diagnostic need, or collecting additional samples? · Outline any plans for long-term monitoring/follow-up. · If the study involves the use of any ionising radiation (e.g. x-rays) or non-ionising radiation, such as MRI scans. · If a participant may need reasonable accommodations or communication support to take part, explain what support is available and how it can be requested. · If audio or visual recordings are used, explain why they are needed, whether recording is required or optional, who will use/access the recordings, and whether the participant may decline recording in their specific case where this is optional. State whether the participant can review or edit the recording/transcript where applicable.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What will happen to my samples and genetic information? Drafting note: Include this section whenever biological samples are collected, used or stored for the main trial. Remove only if no biological material is involved. State exactly which samples are collected or used, including existing clinical samples where applicable, the amount, when and how they are collected, and whether each sample or test is required for the main trial or genuinely optional. Explain the main-trial purpose, coding/pseudonymisation, storage location and duration, laboratories or other recipients, transfers outside the EEA, security, and whether samples are destroyed, used up or retained only for the approved main-trial purpose after analysis. [Conditional – genetic/genomic testing within the main trial] Explain the type and purpose of genetic testing in plain language; whether it is required or optional; the fact that DNA is unique and cannot be regarded as completely anonymous; foreseeable privacy, family or discrimination risks; whether individual results or incidental findings may be returned and how; any counselling available; storage/security and transfers of genetic material/data; and any relevant commercial involvement. Do not include storage or use for unspecified future or secondary research here. Use the separate Secondary and Future Use template for any activity outside the main-trial purposes.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Are there any benefits to taking part in this research? · Provide information on potential benefits if any, to the participant or others, through taking part. · If there is no direct benefit to the participant, then this should be stated. SAMPLE TEXT: Taking part in this study will not directly benefit you. However, research performed with your coded/uncoded samples and information may help us to better understand [INSERT RESEARCH AREA] and may result in new tests, drugs or treatment approaches. This is a long-term research project, so the benefits of the research may not be seen for several years. By participating, you are helping to advance science and medicine for future generations.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Are there any risks to me or others if I take part? · This paragraph always applies. Provide a fair and honest evaluation of the possible consequences of key research procedures and drugs. Remember if you mentioned a risk to the research ethics committee, the participants also need to know about it. · Risks, including any discomforts must be clearly explained. All medications have the potential to cause side-effects. Precautions taken to minimise risks should be stated. · The patient should be advised that he/she is entitled to seek a second opinion. · Potential breach of patient confidentiality should be considered as a risk. SAMPLE TEXT (in relation to data risks): Note, there can be considerable variety in respect of data risk, depending on the nature of the study and type of data that is captured and subsequently processed as a consequence. · Health Information (Data): There is a risk that a connection to your identity could be made. Great care will be taken to ensure the confidentiality of all data and the risk to participants of a breach of confidentiality is considered very low [AMEND AS APPROPRIATE]. · [Conditional – include only if genetic or genomic testing is performed] Genetic Testing: There are some risks to genetic testing. The greatest risk is that genetic testing may reveal that you are not related to one or more of your family members, for example we might discover that your father is not the person you expected him to be. There is also the possibility of social and economic disadvantages. Genetic information shared in the wrong way could affect you and your family, such as if an employer or insurance company was to obtain the information. This is termed ‘genetic discrimination’. We will do our utmost to guarantee complete confidentiality, but there is a theoretical risk of this information becoming available to others.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What happens if something goes wrong when I’m taking part in the study? (May not apply) · This paragraph may not apply to your study. · If your study involves a risk and you have measures in place if the risk does materialise, let the participant know; e.g. counselling in case of psychological distress, genetic counselling in case of certain genetic results, referral to a named specialist or named counselling service if something clinically relevant is discovered etc. · If your study is sponsored by a company, and they have signed an indemnity agreement, let the participant know. SAMPLE TEXT: In the unlikely event that you are harmed in any way, the researchers on this study are covered by insurance through [INSERT DETAIL]. This insurance will cover you if you are injured as a result of taking part in this study.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What other treatments are available to me? (May not apply) · Outline any alternative treatments if relevant including the option not to treat.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Will I be told the outcome of the study? Will I be told the results of any tests or investigations performed as part of this study that relate to me? · Provide clarification whether: · Any outcome from the research that would impact directly or indirectly on the participant’s health will be reported to him/her. · The results of the research will be reported to the participant. · Important items to address in this section include: · How the results of the research will be disseminated e.g. medical journals, medical conferences. SAMPLE TEXT: The results of the study will be reported in medical/scientific journals and disclosed at medical/scientific conferences. No information which reveals your identity will be disclosed.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Part 2 – Data Protection The following information should also be included as standard in Participant Information Leaflets, in order to ensure compliance with the 2018 Health Research Regulations. What information about me (personal data) will be used as part of this study? Will my medical records be accessed? Provide a description of the personal data to be collected and used. List each item you intend to record. · Important items to address in this section include: · Whether the participant’s medical records will be accessed. · Why identifiable data rather than anonymised data is required.
template_content.section_style: Section break, H2 document subline, H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What will happen to my personal data? Outline what will happen to the participant’s personal data. Include details of other data controllers, data processors, third parties that will have access to the personal data. · Confirm that arrangements are in place so that personal data will be processed only as is necessary to achieve the objective of the health research and will not be processed in a way that damage or distress will be caused to the participant. · State the length of time the personal data will be kept (in an identifiable or pseudonymised format) and why it is necessary to keep it for that period. · State the arrangements to be made for the personal data to be archived or destroyed. · State whether the personal data collected will leave the State and if so what countries it will go to and why it is going to those countries. · If applicable, state the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling and information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject. · State how long the signed Consent Form will be retained and why. If its retention period differs from the research data, explain this separately. · If personal data are transferred outside the EEA, identify the receiving organisation(s) and country/countries and explain in simple terms the safeguards used to protect the participant’s data and privacy rights. Avoid unnecessary operational detail in the participant-facing text.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Who will access and use my personal data as part of this study? · Name the individuals (i.e. PI, Co-Investigator, TCD/SJH study team etc.) who will access (or have access to) the participant’s personal data as part of this study including those who will access their medical records (if relevant). · Identify any healthcare providers or other persons from whom personal data will be sought. · Specify any person to whom it is intended to disclose the personal data collected (whether in an identifiable, pseudonymised or anonymised form). · Will the data leave the site/Ireland/ the EU?
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Will my personal data be kept confidential? How will my data be kept safe? Outline the confidentiality and security measures in relation to the participant’s data. · Describe the data security arrangements in place. · Confirm that a Risk Assessment of the data protection implications of the health research and /or a Data Protection Impact Assessment was carried out and an indication of the level of risk identified by either or both. · State whether any presentation or publication in relation to the study could identify the participant. · Confirm that the persons carrying out the research or otherwise having access to the personal data are bound by a professional code of secrecy (like doctors) or a contractual code of secrecy (that would mean disciplinary action for employees who disclosed or facilitated unauthorised access to the personal data) or some other arrangement that emphasises confidentiality (this may be applicable in the case of medical students). · Confirm that training in data protection law and practice has been provided to those individuals involved in carrying out the research. SAMPLE TEXT: Your privacy is important to us. We take many steps to make sure that we protect your confidentiality and keep your data safe. Here are some examples of how we do this: However, if something did go wrong we ….. · Where applicable, explain any limits to confidentiality, for example where disclosure may be necessary because of a serious risk of harm, a professional duty, legal process or Garda investigation. Explain, where possible, how the participant would be informed about the action taken.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What is the lawful basis to use my personal data? State the lawful basis for the use of the participant’s personal data. · Identify the lawful basis for the processing of data by reference to Article 6 and Article 9 of the GDPR. SAMPLE TEXT: By law, we can use your personal information for scientific research in the public interest. [Insert the study-specific lawful bases under Articles 6 and 9 of the GDPR.] We will also ask for your explicit consent to use your data where required for this health research.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text, Footnote/small text

template_content.section_content: What are my rights? You are entitled to: · The right to access to your data and receive a copy of it · The right to restrict or object to processing of your data · The right to object to any further processing of the information we hold about you (except where it is de-identified) · The right to have inaccurate information about you corrected or deleted · The right to receive your data in a portable format and to have it transferred to another data controller · The right to request deletion of your data By law you can exercise the following rights in relation to your personal data, unless the request would make it impossible or very difficult to conduct the research. You can exercise these rights by contacting [insert study contact details] or the Data Protection Officer at [insert organisation and contact details].
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Part 3 – Costs, Funding and Approval Has this study been approved by a research ethics committee? Provide details of the research ethics committee that gave ethical approval to the research including: · The name and contact details of the committee that gave ethical approval to the research (does not need to be a named individual); · Whether any of the persons carrying out the research have a link to the committee or the institution behind the committee; · The date ethical approval was given by the committee; · Reporting arrangements agreed with the committee; · Any conditions attached to the research by the committee. SAMPLE TEXT: Yes, this study has been approved by [insert name of Research Ethics Committee]. Approval was granted on [INSERT DATE].
template_content.section_style: Section break, H2 document subline, H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Who is organising and funding this study? Will the results be used for commercial purposes? Outline the funding for the study Questions to consider answering in this paragraph: · Who is conducting the research? · Who is funding the research? · Are you getting a grant to do this research? · Are you conducting the research for the purposes of obtaining an academic qualification? · Is a pharmaceutical company funding this study? · Are you being paid to recruit patients to this study? · Will the results be disclosed for commercial purposes? · Disclose relevant industry or other third-party involvement and explain whether the sponsor, researchers, collaborators or commercial partners may benefit from the research or its results. If participant data or samples will be shared with such parties, describe that sharing consistently in the relevant data/sample sections.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Is there any payment for taking part? Will it cost me anything if I agree to take part? State the costs of participation and any reimbursements or compensation to be provided (if any). SAMPLE TEXT: No, we are not paying patients to take part in the study. However, you will be reimbursed for travel expenses if you need to make any visits that you would not normally have made as part of your routine clinical care.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Part 4 – Further Information Who should I contact for information or complaints? If you have any concerns or questions, you can contact: · Principal Investigator: [INSERT CONTACT DETAILS HERE]. · Data Protection Officer: [INSERT NAME/ROLE AND CONTACT DETAILS]. Under GDPR, if you are not satisfied with how your data is being processed, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Commission, 21 Fitzwilliam Square South, Dublin 2, Ireland. Website: www.dataprotection.ie.
template_content.section_style: H2 document subline, H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Will I be contacted again? State whether and when the study team will contact the participant again for study visits, safety follow-up, clinically relevant findings or study results. If the participant wishes to take part, explain the next consent step and that they will receive a copy of the information leaflet and signed Consent Form.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Standard table, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: CONSENT FORM – participant assisted by an impartial witness Required acknowledgements Drafting note: Keep only statements that apply. Delete non-applicable conditional statements. Do not use Yes/No choices or initials for required acknowledgements. Place one confirmation checkbox beside each applicable required acknowledgement. Study title: [INSERT DETAILS] Participant name / study ID: [INSERT DETAILS] By signing below, I confirm that: ☐ The Participant Information Leaflet and Consent Form have been read and explained to me in a way I can understand. I have had enough time to decide and my questions have been answered. ☐ I understand that taking part is voluntary and that I may stop at any time without giving a reason or losing my usual care. ☐ I give informed consent to take part in this study after being informed about what participation involves, including the relevant risks, possible benefits and alternatives. ☐ I understand how my personal data will be used for this study and how my privacy and confidentiality will be protected. [Default – include for a capable participant unless an approved Irish alternative/consent-declaration route applies] ☐ I give explicit consent for my health data to be processed for the research described in the Participant Information Leaflet. [Conditional – required medical-record access] ☐ I give permission for the required access to relevant medical records described in the Participant Information Leaflet. [Conditional – required biological samples] ☐ I agree to the required collection, use and storage of biological samples described in the Participant Information Leaflet. [Conditional – required genetic/genomic testing] ☐ I agree to the required genetic/genomic testing described in the Participant Information Leaflet. [Conditional – other required study procedure] ☐ [INSERT REQUIRED STUDY-SPECIFIC ACKNOWLEDGEMENT]. ☐ I will receive a copy of the Participant Information Leaflet and signed Consent Form.
template_content.section_style: Section break, H2 document subline, H3 module title, Rich body text, Checkbox group

template_content.section_content: Optional choices You may answer “No” to any choice below without refusing the main activity covered by this Consent Form. Drafting note: Include only genuinely optional components that can be refused without preventing the main activity covered by this form. [Conditional – optional biological sample/test within the main trial] I agree to the optional [sample/test] described in the Participant Information Leaflet. Yes ☐ No ☐ [Conditional – optional genetic/genomic testing within the main trial] I agree to the optional genetic/genomic testing described in the Participant Information Leaflet. Yes ☐ No ☐ [Conditional – optional audio/visual recording] I agree to the optional audio and/or visual recording described in the Participant Information Leaflet. Yes ☐ No ☐ [Add other genuinely optional main-trial procedures or permissions only where applicable.] [Conditional – include when one or more optional choices are present] Confirmation of optional choices The optional choices marked above reflect my decisions. Participant name: ____________________ Participant signature/mark (if possible): ____________________ Date: __________ Alternative method of recording confirmation (if unable to sign): ____________________ Impartial witness name: ____________________ Date: __________ Signature: ____________________
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text, Checkbox group, Signature section

template_content.section_content: Participant decision and witness attestation Drafting note: The participant makes every required and optional choice. If the participant can sign, they should sign. If they cannot sign, record the approved alternative method used to document their consent. Participant name: ____________________ Participant signature/mark (if possible): ____________________ Date: __________ Alternative method of recording participant consent (if unable to sign): [INSERT] Impartial witness I confirm that I attended the entire consent discussion, the information was accurately read and explained, the participant appeared to understand it, and the participant freely communicated their own decision and choices. Witness name: ____________________ Relationship/independence from trial: ____________________ Date: __________ Signature: ____________________ Person taking consent Name: ____________________ Role/qualification: ____________________ Date: __________ Signature: ____________________ A signed copy or equivalent consent record and the information leaflet should be provided to the participant.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text, Signature section
